methods.label: Measure both grades in equal units
methods.explanation:
Each buddy pair contains one sixth grader and one ninth grader, so the number of students with buddies is the same in each grade.

Use one fifth of the sixth-grade population as one unit. There are \(5\) units of sixth graders, and \(2\) of those units have buddies. Therefore \(2\) units of ninth graders also have buddies. Since that is one third of the ninth-grade population, the whole ninth grade contains \(3\cdot2=6\) units.

Altogether there are \(5+6=11\) units of students, of which \(2+2=4\) units have buddies. Because every unit represents the same number of students, the requested fraction is
\[
\frac{4}{11}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Equal groups make the whole-from-part relationships visible using elementary fractions and ratios, without formal algebra.
